fieldworkDocument.title: Measgaichte / Miscellaneous
fieldworkDocument.note: [NOTES: the words have been slipped and therefore, apart from the definitions provided by Mr Morrison, the definitions as they appear on the slips have also been included (unless the two were the same).]

item.description: an eight pound hammer for striking the hand drill.
claw hammer.
a cow for the slaughter, or a cow for slaughtering.
wallowed. Air a luidreadh anns a’ pholl. [SLIP: Wallowing.]
waving to a person (colloquially spelt). Perhaps you may spell it smèideadh. I spelt it here the way it is pronounced on Scalpay. [SLIP: Phonetic spelling of ‘smèideadh’ – waving.]
a movement of teeth, striking against one another as in the cold. [SLIP: Chattering (of teeth with the cold).]
slab [slap?], slab [slap?] in the face.
non stop, very talkative person. Cha deachaidh fuaradh air o thàinig sinn an seo an diugh – referring to a talkative person. (Scalpay)
stitch.
hold on. Greimich ris.
pain. Greim ’na thaobh. (Scalpay)
swearing. Rinn e ’n sgrùdadh sin dha. (Scalpay)
(also) a flighty female.
laugh, loud laugh, guffaw.
laughing loudly, convulsive laughing. (Scalpay)
wasn’t enough seen, without going any further, Scalpay version.
fun. [NOTES: the slip has ‘dibhearsain’.]
nausea, feeling sea-sick.
peeping.
beam, ray, ray of sunshine.
Cha do gheàrr e sgiobhadh [sic] – he didn’t move a limb. (Scalpay) [SLIP: ‘He didn’t move a muscle’.]
tremble, alternative perhaps [see sgiofadh]. Cha do gheàrr e crith.
little time. Cha dean thu sin ann an sgiorraig. (Scalpay)
bite, bit. Cha d’fhuair sinn fiochd. [SLIP: Bite.]
[See fiochd] but perhaps not quite, as fiochd may have developed from fiach etc. Piochd of the nibbling portion, morsel size. [SLIP: See ‘fiochd’. Also nibble, morsel, portion.]
pleasuring, boating or boating for pleasure.
plating, plaster. Phlac e air a mhuin e. (Scalpay) [NOTES: slipped under ‘placadh’ and ‘plac’.]
lukewarm (Scalpay). Burn flodach. [NOTES: the slip has ‘bùrn flodach’.]
wreckage.
deficiency. Tha ’n fhàgail sin air.
picking.
sale. Tha e dha rup – putting it on sale, or offering it for sale. [SLIP: Up for sale.]
untidy. Tha e neo i cho rablach – so untidy.
race. Raoidhs aice ’dol seachad air an uinneig.
quietly. Chaidh e stigh cho fiaite (spelt colloquially) ’s a b’ urrain dha. I doubt if it’s the same as fiata?
